body:
## Pull request overview This PR disables key expiry for tagged nodes to match Tailscale's behavior. Tagged nodes (registered with tagged PreAuthKeys or via --advertise-tags) now have their expiry set to nil during initial registration. On re-authentication, tagged nodes preserve their disabled expiry while user-owned nodes can update their expiry from client requests. **Changes:** - Tagged nodes created with PreAuthKeys or advertise-tags now have key expiry disabled (set to nil) - Re-authentication logic for tagged nodes preserves the disabled expiry setting - Comprehensive test coverage added for tagged/untagged expiry behavior and re-authentication scenarios ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | hscontrol/state/state.go | Added logic to disable expiry for tagged nodes during creation and preserve disabled expiry during PreAuthKey re-authentication | | hscontrol/auth_tags_test.go | Added comprehensive tests for expiry behavior with tagged/untagged nodes and re-authentication scenarios |
Comments suppressed due to low confidence (1) **hscontrol/state/state.go:1325** * The OIDC/CLI re-registration flow in HandleNodeFromAuthPath does not preserve disabled expiry for tagged nodes. This is inconsistent with the PreAuthKey re-authentication logic (lines 1552-1556) which correctly checks IsTagged() before updating expiry. Tagged nodes registered via advertise-tags that re-authenticate through OIDC/CLI will incorrectly have their expiry updated. Add the same IsTagged() check here to preserve disabled expiry for tagged nodes. ``` if expiry != nil { node.Expiry = expiry } else { node.Expiry = regEntry.Node.Expiry } ```
